title: A healthy snack under ₹20
body: College students want a filling, healthy snack they can buy at the campus shop for under ₹20. Most options are fried chips or biscuits.

title: Office tea-time snack
body: Office workers in Tier-1 cities buy a snack with their 4 pm tea every day, but say the choices are oily and leave them sluggish.

title: School tiffin filler
body: Parents of 6–12-year-olds want a packed snack for the school tiffin that is not junk, costs under ₹15 and survives a hot bag till lunch.

title: Travel snack for bus journeys
body: People on long bus journeys buy snacks at highway stops; packs are often stale, overpriced and messy to eat in a moving bus.

title: Protein for gym beginners
body: Young people starting at the gym want more protein, but protein bars cost ₹80 or more and taste chalky.

title: Diabetic-friendly namkeen
body: Families with a diabetic member want namkeen everyone can share at tea time without worrying about sugar or refined flour.

title: Regional snack for city migrants
body: Students and workers who moved from their home state miss a regional snack that city shops do not stock.

title: Late-night hostel hunger
body: Hostel students get hungry after midnight when the mess is closed; instant noodles are the only thing the night canteen sells.

title: Summer drink for outdoor workers
body: Delivery riders and construction workers spend hours in the heat; soft drinks are sugary and coconut water is expensive.

title: Low-sugar drink for kids
body: Parents want a drink for children's birthday parties that kids like but that is not loaded with sugar.

title: Ready-to-drink chai
body: Commuters want a decent cup of chai on the go; station tea is unhygienic and cafe chai costs ₹80.

title: Sports drink for village cricket
body: Teenagers playing cricket in small towns want an energy drink; imported sports drinks cost too much and are hard to find.

title: Hangover-free party mixer
body: Young adults at house parties want a tasty non-alcoholic drink so the person driving home is not left out.

title: Morning drink instead of coffee
body: Students who drink three coffees a day want something that keeps them alert without the jitters and the evening crash.

title: Buttermilk that lasts
body: People love chaas with lunch, but packed buttermilk spoils quickly outside the fridge and tastes flat.

title: Curd for small fridges
body: Single working people buy a 400 g curd tub, use half and throw the rest away when it turns sour.

title: Lactose-free milk for tea
body: Many adults get stomach trouble from milk but still want milky tea; lactose-free milk costs twice as much and few shops stock it.

title: Paneer that stays fresh
body: Home cooks buy paneer on weekends but it goes rubbery or sour within two days in the fridge.

title: Five-minute breakfast for students
body: Students skip breakfast because cooking takes too long; cereal is sugary and costs ₹200 a box.

title: Ready poha or upma
body: Working couples want a home-style breakfast like poha on weekdays but have no time to chop and cook in the morning.

title: Millet breakfast for families
body: Doctors keep recommending millets, but families find them hard to cook and children refuse to eat them.

title: Soap for hard water
body: In many towns the water is hard; soap does not lather and leaves skin dry and itchy.

title: Sunscreen for two-wheeler riders
body: College students who ride scooters every day get tanned and burnt, but sunscreen feels greasy and costs ₹300 or more.

title: Men's face wash under ₹50
body: Young men in small towns want a face wash for oily skin and pimples; branded ones cost over ₹150.

title: Sanitary pads for rural girls
body: Girls in villages often miss school during their periods because pads are expensive and hard to buy discreetly.

title: Hair oil that is not sticky
body: Young people want the benefits of hair oil their parents swear by, but hate the sticky look in college or office.

title: Deodorant for humid cities
body: In humid coastal cities deodorants fade by noon and people sweat through their shirts on the commute.

title: Toothpaste for sensitive teeth
body: Many people avoid cold drinks and ice cream because of sensitive teeth; specialist toothpastes cost over ₹150.

title: Baby care at a small-town price
body: Young parents in small towns want gentle baby lotion and wipes; trusted brands cost too much for daily use.

title: Dishwash for hard water
body: Dish soaps leave white spots on steel utensils in hard-water areas, and cooks scrub twice.

title: Mosquito repellent without smoke
body: Families want protection from mosquitoes at night, but coils make the room smoky and children cough.

title: Laundry for small loads
body: Students washing clothes by hand in hostels buy a 1 kg detergent pack and it lasts months, caking in the humidity.

title: Floor cleaner safe for pets
body: Pet owners worry that strong floor cleaners harm dogs and cats that lick the floor.

title: Kitchen grease remover
body: Indian kitchens with daily tadka build up sticky grease on tiles and exhaust fans that ordinary cleaners do not shift.

title: Air freshener for small flats
body: People in small flats without windows in the bathroom want the space to smell fresh without harsh chemicals.

title: Ready masala for bachelors
body: Young people living alone want home-style dal and sabzi but do not know which spices to mix.

title: Atta that makes soft rotis
body: New cooks struggle to make soft rotis; their rotis turn hard within minutes.

title: Small packs of ghee
body: Families in small towns want pure ghee for festivals but can only afford small amounts at a time; small packs are rare.

title: Instant meals for night shifts
body: Call-centre and hospital staff on night shifts eat whatever the canteen has; they want a filling hot meal they can make in minutes.

title: Healthy cooking oil
body: Families worry about heart health but healthier oils cost much more than the usual refined oil.

title: Sugar-free mithai for festivals
body: During festivals families want to share sweets with elderly relatives who are told to avoid sugar.

title: Chocolate that survives the heat
body: Chocolates melt in shop shelves and school bags in Indian summers, so small shops stop stocking them from April.

title: Mithai that travels
body: People visiting relatives in other cities want to carry mithai, but it gets crushed or spoils in a day.

title: Iron for young women
body: Many young women are anaemic; iron tablets taste bad and cause stomach trouble, so they stop taking them.

title: ORS that children will drink
body: Children with diarrhoea refuse to drink plain ORS because of its salty taste, and parents give up.

title: Immunity drink for monsoon
body: Families get colds every monsoon and want a daily drink that helps, without bitter kadha.

title: Affordable dog food
body: Families in towns who adopt street dogs feed them leftovers because branded dog food costs ₹300 a kilo.

title: Crayons that are safe to chew
body: Toddlers put crayons in their mouths; parents worry about chemicals in cheap crayons.

title: Healthy snack for picky eaters
body: Parents of picky eaters want a snack with hidden vegetables or millets that children actually finish.

title: Pens that last a semester
body: College students lose or run out of pens every week; a refillable pen costs too much and a cheap one leaks in exams.
